messages:
Priya: Quick thread: proposing a hybrid 'slot-continuum' autoscaling policy for Dedicated GPU pools. Idea: combine fixed-slot reservations for latency-critical tenants + a soft continuum for opportunistic burst. Goal: reduce cold-starts while keeping utilization high.
Ethan: Can you sketch how continuum differs from current burst-credit model?
Priya: continuum = continuous fractional allocation instead of discrete slot grants. Each tenant has min_slots (hard) and continuum_weight. Runtime maps continuum_weight -> probabilistic fractional admission, aggregated into actual slices per GPU. Think of it as token-bucket with fractional tokens.
Jess: fractional allocations sound neat but worried about packing complexity on MIG/NVIDIA fractional GPUs. Do we have placement algorithm to stitch fractions efficiently?
Priya: placement plan: allocator builds 'fractional bins' per GPU that track used_fraction. Admission tries to fit new request into existing bins with slack >= request_fraction. If none, try split across 2 bins (with penalty) or allocate a full slot from reserved pool.
Rao: penalty on split increases latency and KV-cache misses. We should quantify p99 impact vs utilization gains.
Priya: agree, propose metrics: p99_lat_split, avg_kv_miss_rate, utilization_by_gpu_type. We'll simulate with 30 days of traces.
Ethan: How do we decide request_fraction? Depends on model context length and batch shape. Need a lightweight estimator in admit path.
Priya: admission estimator = ceil(tokens/1024) * base_fraction * model_factor. Keep it cheap: single CPU op. We can refine offline.
Jess: also need tenant QoS tiers: latency-critical tenants get guaranteed min_slots + prefer same-GPU packing for affinity. Opportunistic tenants accept split/shredded placements.
Priya: yes. Policy knobs: min_slots, continuum_weight, split_penalty_ms, max_splits_per_request. Default min_slots=1 for premium, 0 for standard.
scale-bot: recorded feature flag: feature.hybrid_slot_continuum = off by default.
Ethan: fallback behavior? If continuum overcommits under thermal or preemption pressure, how do we gracefully degrade?
Priya: degrade plan: 1) degrade continuum weight proportionally with global headroom signal, 2) prioritize freeing shards from opportunistic tenants first, 3) trigger proactive prewarm for premium tenants if we detect increasing queue depth.
Rao: eviction semantics matter. Opportunistic shards should be preemptible without full request aborts. Add a preempt callback that returns a graceful shutdown window (e.g., 200ms) to let do-inflight token flushing.
Jess: are we comfortable adding that small blocking window to serving runtime? It could complicate tail-latency guarantees.
Priya: keep it optional per tenant. premium tenants set preempt_window=0 (non-preemptible). Opportunistic default 200ms.
Ethan: rollout strategy? This is risky: new packing + placement changes.
Priya: rollout plan: 1) simulator + perf model on historical traces (must show <1% p99 regressions for premium), 2) internal-only canary on staging cluster, 3) 5% tenant canary with opportunistic flag enabled, 4) 25% with continuum validation mode (dual-accounting), 5) full enable for opportunistic after 2 weeks stable.
Jess: suggest we enable continuum_readonly mode first where allocator computes continuum placements but doesn't execute them; used for metric comparisons.
Priya: good call. continuum_readonly + dual-accounting will catch surprises.
Rao: metrics to watch: premium_p99, split_rate, gpu_util_pct, preempt_evictions_per_min, kv_miss_delta. Also add alarms for >0.5% increase in premium_p99 over baseline.
Priya: add these to dashboards. Ethan, can you own dashboard panels?
Ethan: yep. I'll add panels and a comparative view vcurrent vs vcontinuum.
scale-bot: created alert: premium_p99_delta > 0.5% over 1h => notify #eng-runtime-oncall.
Priya: security/compliance note: no tenant data moves across GPUs differently. Placement doesn't change data residency; ops team ok?
Rao: fine, just ensure placement logs include tenant_id hashes only, not raw IDs.
Jess: implementation tasks: API surface change (admit request includes optional estimate fields), allocator changes (fractional bins), runtime preempt window, stats & dashboards, simulator. We should produce a short RFC doc.
Priya: I'll start an RFC draft. Jess/Ethan/Rao volunteer for implementation owners?
Jess: I'll do allocator & runtime changes (placement + preempt).
Ethan: I'll do metrics/dashboards + simulator ingestion.
Rao: I can wire ops flags, feature gating, and alerting.
Priya: timeline: RFC this week, simulator + initial perf run next week, staging canary in 3 weeks.
ops-bot: Reminder: please post RFC link in #eng-docs and add owners to the RFC template.
Priya: thanks everyone. I'll ping when RFC PR is ready. :rocket:
